captions.instagram:
Working on OPT or CPT? Look at your pay stub for Social Security and Medicare (FICA).

✔️ F-1 and J-1 students who are nonresident aliens are generally exempt on work USCIS authorizes, including practical training like OPT and CPT.
✔️ The exemption generally ends once you're a resident for tax purposes (often after 5 calendar years) or switch to a status like H-1B.
✔️ Withheld by mistake? Ask your employer to return it first.
✔️ If they won't return all of it, file Form 843 with Form 8316 and your documents.

Tax information only, not immigration advice. We prepare the Social Security/Medicare claim (Forms 843 + 8316) for $49, and e-file Form 1040-NR + 8843 in our student package ($99 federal, $129 with one state return). Book a call to start. Not available for CA, CT, MD, NY or OR state returns.

sources.fact: F-1, J-1, M-1 nonresident alien students are exempt from Social Security and Medicare on USCIS-authorized employment, including practical training; F-2/J-2/M-2 not exempt; exemption ends on change to non-exempt status or becoming a resident alien (generally after 5 calendar years); if withheld in error, ask the employer, then Form 843 with Form 8316 (read 2026-10-24)
Employer must start withholding FICA on the effective date of the H-1B status change (often Oct. 1) (read 2026-10-24)
OPT = Optional Practical Training (practical training authorized for F-1 students)
